meta.title: Safari Zone
meta.description: The hub's Safari Zone: the 60-slot Pokémon pool (slots 0–44 regular, 45–59 legendary), the four ways Pokémon enter it, the temporary illegal ribbon that gates every push, the priority and eviction system that decides who stays, and the Legends Cave flow for re-battling the legendaries you've caught. All of the mechanics are identical between Vanilla and EX — what differs is which legendary species exist to catch.

prose.heading: The Safari Zone in the hub
prose.text: The Safari Area is one of the four hub areas that already exists when you start, always attached to the Town Exit (which is itself attached to the Labs) — so the zone is always two hops from the Labs and never directly next to them. Its introduction tutorial plays the first time you visit. The zone is a catch practice ground for the Pokémon of your own save: up to 6 of the pooled Pokémon are visible in the grass at a time, battles are safari-style catch battles (you pick which ball to throw from your bag mid-battle), and a sign in the area lets you view the current regular pool in a special Pokédex view or “Dismiss” all regular Pokémon at once.

prose.heading: The 60-slot pool
prose.text: Beyond the 60 slots, a 16-entry “custom data” table — not 16 additional Pokémon slots — lets unique/gift Pokémon keep their special sets while they sit in the pool. A temporary “illegal ribbon” (the code reuses the Marine ribbon slot) is what gates every push into the pool: a mon is only added if it does not carry the ribbon, and every successful push stamps it — so the same mon can't be added twice. The ribbon is also stamped on every member of your pre-run party and every Day Care mon at the start of every run — that is what keeps your home team out of the pool (see The run-start illegal ribbon). (An outdated comment in the constants says “45–49 are for legends”, but every allocation and reset loop in the code uses the full 45–59 range.)

prose.heading: How Pokémon enter the pool
prose.text: Four events push Pokémon into the pool — two while a run is active, one when the run ends, and a low-priority discard path. Every push goes through the same gate — the run-start illegal ribbon — detailed after the four cards.

prose.heading: Priority and eviction
prose.text: Eviction is not a fixed batch size: when a range is full, the code finds the lowest priority value, evicts every mon sitting on it, and subtracts that same value from every survivor's priority. A 0-minimum therefore evicts the 0-priority entrants and leaves everything else unchanged, and with priorities 5, 5 and 30 the two 5s go while the 30 becomes 25. A discarded catch — caught and immediately released — enters at 0, the same score a mon released without gaining a level earns, so they share the eviction line; a shiny's +30 is no guarantee either, because a mon that has gained 78 or more levels already scores above it.

prose.heading: The Legends Cave
prose.text: Completing the “True Legend” quest (catch a legendary during an adventure) grants the hidden “Legend Cave” upgrade, which puts a cave entrance on the Safari Area. From there, 10 Pokéblocks of a single standard type the pooled legendary has — ten of the same block, not ten assorted ones — are turned into a wild, catchable battle with that legendary, and the statue deducts them the moment you pick the block to spend.

records.name: Released from your party
records.short: Mid-run — releasing a mon pushes it straight in.
records.description: While a run is active, releasing a Pokémon from your party immediately pushes it into the pool (except during the endless trainer mode after the top of the boss ladder) — if the mon isn't wearing its run-start illegal ribbon — and it is also copied to the fainted-mon lab, where a lab encounter can offer it back. A released pre-run party mon wears the ribbon, so the pool push is skipped — only the lab copy is made — and it comes back with the rest of your pre-run party when the run ends. Legendaries go to the legendary slots, everything else to the regular slots.

records.name: Fainted and removed mid-run
records.short: Mid-run — with the release setting on, 0-HP party mons are pushed out after a win.
records.description: With the “Release Fainted Pokémon” setting on, any party Pokémon left at 0 HP after a battle you win in a run is removed from your party. A run-acquired mon goes two places: it is pushed into the pool — same as a release, gated by the run-start illegal ribbon — and it is copied to the fainted-mon lab, where a lab encounter can offer it back. A fainted pre-run party mon wears the ribbon, so the pool push is skipped — only the lab copy is made — and the original comes back with the rest of your pre-run party when the run ends. Removal is skipped entirely (fainted mons stay in the party) if the setting is off, or the run is past the top of the boss ladder, at the final-champion stage while the final quest's effect is active, or the run is a postgame replay.

records.name: When the run ends
records.short: Run end — the run-acquired party, then the Day Care, is added.
records.description: When an adventure ends (victory or defeat), every Pokémon in your party that isn't wearing its run-start illegal ribbon is added to the pool — in practice, the mons you picked up during the run — and then the same for your Day Care. Your pre-run party and Day Care wear the ribbon, so they are skipped and instead restored from the pre-run snapshot the run took of your hub state — a run you lose still returns your team as it was, and only the mons you picked up during the run restock the Safari Zone. Edge case: the Starter Bag upgrade hands you your random starter after the snapshot but before the ribbon stamping, so a starter that survives the whole run is neither added to the pool (it carries the ribbon) nor restored to your party (it isn't in the snapshot) — it is lost entirely.

records.name: Discarded after capture
records.short: Per catch — a discarded catch enters at priority 0.
records.description: If you catch a wild Pokémon and choose to discard it instead of keeping it, it is pushed into the pool at priority 0 — the same score a mon released without gaining a level earns, so a discard shares the eviction line with any other 0-priority mon and goes out with the first eviction its range sees. A shiny discard earns the +30 shiny bonus instead, though even that is no guarantee of outranking a mon that has gained 78 or more levels. (During a catching contest, non-shiny discards are skipped entirely.)
records.source: src/battle_script_commands.c @vanilla L10283-10300 (rogue_caughtmon battle command) / @origin/expansion L15521-15538; src/rogue_controller.c @vanilla L1335-1350 / @origin/expansion L1335-1350 (Rogue_DiscardedCaughtMon, push at L1343); src/rogue_safari.c @vanilla L107-118 / @origin/expansion L107-118 (RogueSafari_PushLowPriorityMon)

records.name: The run-start illegal ribbon
records.short: A temp ribbon gates every push — pre-run mons are stamped at run start, so only run-acquired mons can enter.
records.description: Every push into the pool first checks the mon's temporary illegal ribbon (the code reuses the Marine ribbon slot): a mon carrying it is skipped, and every successful push stamps it, so a given mon can enter the pool at most once. At the start of every run — after the run has snapshotted your pre-run hub state (party, Day Care, bag and money) and, with the Starter Bag upgrade, handed out your random starter — the ribbon is stamped on every member of the current party and on every Day Care mon. That snapshot is what your hub state is restored to when the run ends, so pre-run mons can never enter the pool: they simply come back, and a pre-run mon released or fainted mid-run goes to the lab instead of the pool. Two other paths stamp the ribbon mid-run: picking up a mon from the lab (the stamp stops it re-entering the pool if it got there when it fainted) and snagging a trainer mon under the Snag Curse. The edge case this creates: your Starter Bag starter is handed out after the snapshot but before the stamping, so a starter that survives the whole run is neither added to the pool (it carries the ribbon) nor restored to your party (it isn't in the snapshot) — the Pokémon is lost entirely. A snagged trainer mon that survives to run end meets the same fate.

records.name: Slot layout (60 pool slots)
records.description: The pool is exactly 60 slots: 0–44 are regular slots (45 total — the only slots the open zone spawns from, cycling through them in order), and 45–59 are legendary slots (15 total — reachable only via the Legends Cave). A separate 16-entry “custom data” table — not 16 extra Pokémon slots — maps unique/gift Pokémon so they keep their special sets while pooled. (The in-code comment “45-49 are for legends” is outdated; the allocation, reset and any-legends loops all use 45–59.)
records.source: include/constants/rogue.h @vanilla L806-810 / @origin/expansion L808-812 (ROGUE_SAFARI_TOTAL_MONS 60, LEGENDS_START_INDEX 45, TOTAL_CUSTOM_MONS 16); src/rogue_safari.c @vanilla L313-375 / @origin/expansion L313-375 (AllocSafariMonSlotFor: regular → 0..44, legendary → 45..59)

records.name: Priority and eviction
records.description: Each entry's priority is (levels gained since capture × 2) ÷ 5; a discarded catch enters at 0; shinies add a flat +30 (half the 60-slot pool size); and any IV bonus from IV-boosting charms is stripped before the mon is stored. When a range (regular or legendary) is full, the code evicts every mon sharing the lowest priority value — a batch whose size depends on the tie — and subtracts that lowest value, not the batch size, from every surviving priority: with priorities 5, 5 and 30, both 5s go and the 30 becomes 25, while a 0-minimum costs survivors nothing. Regular and legendary ranges evict independently and never evict each other. Custom-data eviction is separate: the shared 16-entry custom-data table (not 16 extra pool slots) keeps the special sets of unique and gift mons, and when it is full, admitting another custom set evicts the lowest-priority mon already holding a custom entry — which can sit in the other range even when the destination range has a free slot.

score.note: the IV bonus from IV-boosting charms is stripped before the mon is stored

eviction: A range (regular or legendary) is full
Every mon sharing the lowest priority value is evicted as a batch
Every survivor's priority drops by that lowest value, not the batch size
One freed slot takes the new arrival
records.source: src/rogue_safari.c @vanilla L37-92 (PushBoxMonInternal: priority at L82, charm strip at L48, shiny +30 at L88), L313-375 (eviction batching in AllocSafariMonSlotFor) and L376-440 (custom-data eviction in AllocCustomMonSafariSlot) / @origin/expansion L37-92, L313-375, L376-440

records.name: Legends Cave legendary catch
steps: Complete the “True Legend” quest (catch a legendary during an adventure) — its reward is the hidden “Legend Cave” upgrade, which adds the cave entrance to the Safari Area.
Enter the cave and talk to the odd statue. If no legendaries are in the pool, “the cave is silent.”
Choose “Make Offering” from the statue menu.
Pick the legendary you want from the special Pokédex view of your pooled legendaries.

The offering is 10 Pokéblocks of a single standard type, and that type must be one of the legendary's two types — ten Water Pokéblocks for a Water-type legendary. It takes ten of the same block, not ten assorted blocks.
Choose the block to offer from your bag. If its type isn't one the legendary has, it “won't like that type of Pokéblock.”

The statue deducts the 10 the moment you pick an eligible block with enough stock and scatters them near the statue — there is no confirmation step, and if you have fewer than 10 it says 10 are needed in order to make an offering and spends nothing.
The cave shakes, the legendary-appears theme plays, the cry rings out — and a wild battle with that legendary begins (safari-style, catchable).
records.description: The Legends Cave is how legendaries in the pool (slots 45–59) become re-encounterable: a statue that spends 10 Pokéblocks of a single standard type the legendary likes into a wild battle with the legendary you pick. The offering is a plain spend with no confirmation — the statue deducts the blocks the moment an eligible one is picked — while the statue's other option, “Dismiss Pokémon”, is the destructive one: it asks a final confirm question, and if you agree it empties the entire legendary pool at once. The whole flow is identical between versions — what differs is the roster of legendaries that can exist in the pool, since EX adds every Gen 4–9 legendary, their alternate forms, and the Z-A Floettes on top of Vanilla's Gen 1–3 set.

differences.vanilla: Mechanically identical cave; the catchable legendaries are limited to the Gen 1–3 legendary species (and forms) that exist in the Vanilla build.
differences.ex: Same cave and flow, but the legendary encounter roster adds all Gen 4–9 legendaries, alternate forms and the Z-A Floettes — so far more species can fill slots 45–59.

records.name: View and dismiss the pool
records.description: The sign in the Safari Area offers two actions: “View Pokémon” opens the regular pool (slots 0–44) in a special Pokédex view showing each mon's name, level and shininess, and “Dismiss Pokémon” clears all regular pool entries at once (the Legends Cave has its own separate “Dismiss” for the legendary slots).
